trump isnt the 1st president to want more room to entertain longtime white house usher says breitbart president donald trump is not the first president to want more room at the white house for entertaining says the longestserving top aide in the executive residence offering some backup for the reason trump has cited for his ballroom construction project gary walters spent more than two decades as white house chief usher to presidents ronald reagan george hw bush bill clinton and george w bush a role that is akin to being the general manager of the residence all the presidents that i had an opportunity to serve always talked about some possibility of an enlarged area for entertaining walters said in an interview with the associated press about his recently published memoir trump has been talking about building a white house ballroom for years even before he entered the political arena in july the white house announced a 90000squarefoot space would be built on the east side of the complex to accommodate 650 seated guests at a thenestimated cost of 200 million trump has said it will be paid for with private donations including from him the republican president later upped the proposed ballrooms capacity to 999 people and by october had demolished the twostory east wing of the white house to build it there in december he updated the price tag to 400 million double the original estimate images of the east wing being demolished shocked historians preservationists and others but walters said there is a long history of projects on the campus ranging from conservatories greenhouses and stables being torn down to build the west wing in 1902 to the expansion of the residence with a third floor to the addition of the east wing itself during world war ii to provide workspace for the first lady her staff and other white house offices so theres always been construction going on around the white house walters said other presidents bemoaned the lack of space for entertaining when walters was on the job the capacity of the largest public rooms in the white house was among the first topics he discussed with the incoming president first lady and their social secretary he said the presidents he served all talked about the limited number of people the white house could handle when set up for a state dinner the state dining room can hold about 130 people 13 round tables each with seating for 10 walters said the east room can accommodate about 300 chairs fewer if space is needed for television cameras trump complains often that both rooms are too small he also has complained about the use of large tents on the south grounds the main workaround for big events such as ritzy state dinners for foreign leaders walters said the tents had issues when it rained the water flows downhill and the grass became soggy no matter what we tried to do walters said we dug culverts around the outside of the tent to try and get the water tents damaged the grass requiring more work to reseed it he said walters admitted it was a bit jarring to see the east wing torn down and said he had fond personal memories of the space i met my wife at the white house and she worked in the east wing so that was a joy for me said walters 79 his wife barbara was a receptionist in the visitors office during the administrations of richard nixon and gerald ford the couple recently celebrated 48 years of marriage broken bones alter ushers career trajectory walters owes his place in history as the longestserving white house chief usher to the misfortune of a broken ankle he was 23 in early 1970 honorably discharged from the army and looking for a job that would allow him to finish college at night the executive protective service a precursor to the us secret service was hiring and accepted him but shortly before the graduation ceremony walters broke an ankle playing football he could not patrol out of uniform wearing a cast and hobbling around on crutches so he was given a temporary assignment in the white house police control and appointments center he stayed for five years this injury also changed the course of my career walters wrote in his memoir white house memories 19702007 recollections of the longestserving chief usher he gained an indepth knowledge of the ways and security systems of the white house that would ultimately greatly benefit me in my future role in the ushers office a few months after being promoted to sergeant in 1975 he learned of an opening in the ushers office he applied and joined as an assistant in early 1976 a decade later he was elevated to chief usher by reagan who gave walters the top job in the residence overseeing maintenance construction and renovation projects and food service along with administrative financial and personnel functions he managed a staff of about 90 butlers housekeepers cooks florists electricians engineers plumbers and others walters retired in 2007 after 37 years at the white house including a record 21 years as chief usher he served under seven presidents from nixon to george w bush in that time walters saw a broad swath of presidential history the only president who ever resigned an appointed vice president become the only unelected president a president be impeached and stay in office a father and son become president and the supreme court decide the most closely contested presidential election in us history hes often asked what he liked most about his work and without hesitation i say it is getting to know and interact directly with the president first lady and other members of their family it was an honor to get to know them with my own eyes and ears walters wrote

col jacques baud is the west finally waking up for those who are unaware baud was recently sanctioned by the eu government from kimi k2 the sanctioning of colonel jacques baud a european civilliberties earthquake 00000030 i cannot even buy food the humanitarian cliffedge colonel bauds first words are not about geostrategy but about groceries because every euro dollar or swiss franc that passes through a clearing bank inside the eu is now legally toxic if it touches his name a friend in switzerland cannot order online a box of vegetables to be delivered to his brussels address the payment is blocked at checkout the algorithm recognises the delivery postcode and freezes the transaction in other words a retired swiss officer who has never been charged with let alone convicted of a single crime is being starved by a silent piece of code the eu regulation council decision 20243189 art 2 prohibits making available directly or indirectly any economic resources to a listed person economic resources is left undefined so supermarkets courier firms and even neighbours who might reimburse a pizza delivery assume the strictest interpretation total embargo the belgian treasury has told banks that the humanitarian exemption exists but it is not automatic it must be applied for through the councils working party on sanctions which meets in secret and which over the christmas truce simply does not meet thus a bureaucratic vacuum becomes a weapon baud is free to walk the streets of brussels but he is not free to eat unless strangers physically carry food to his door the ancient legal maxim that the state must feed the prisoner it will not release has been inverted the state has imprisoned the man but outsourced the feeding to neighbours 00300400 i am not allowed to enter the union i live in the juridical black hole the sanctions list was drafted for foreigners russian generals syrian ministers hamas financiers baud is a citizen of switzerland legally resident in belgium holder of a belgian residence card and a swiss passport the council text therefore contains an ontological contradiction it bars him from entering territory where he is already lawfully present belgian administrative courts have no jurisdiction to annul a eu regulation the court of justice in luxembourg does but only after years of procedure and a 50000 advance on lawyers fees money he cannot legally receive the travel ban also prohibits him from leaving for switzerland to collect his pension because the moment he crosses the schengen border he enters again on return and needs an impossible visa he is thus physically marooned inside a polity that claims he is outside it the parallel baud himself draws is with the soviet prophylactic exile of the 1970s the citizen is present but his civic existence is erased eu officials when pressed by german mps reply that the honourable colonel may apply for an authorisation to travel for humanitarian reasons yet the same regulation states that such authorisations must be unanimous in the council where france the state that proposed him can veto without giving reasons due process has been replaced by a kafkacircuit the accused must beg the accuser for the right to beg 04000900 from foreign policy to domestic policing the kgbisation of the eu bauds most serious charge is not military but epistemic he insists that the eu has quietly abolished the 19thcentury liberal distinction between external and internal security the regulation that immobilises him is labelled an eu restrictive measure in view of russias actions destabilising the situation in ukraine official journal l series 2024 in plain language it is a weapons of foreign policy yet the moment it is enforced inside belgium against a resident it mutates into a domestic penal sanction without the safeguards of criminal law no indictment no disclosure of evidence no court no appeal the same intelligence dossier that would once have been handled by a judge in brussels is now processed by the eus intelligence and situation centre eu intcen and sent straight to the council the historical echo baud invokes is the 1954 merger of the soviet mgb foreign intelligence and mvd interior troops into the kgb one bureaucratic tool one legal vocabulary for both the external enemy and the internal dissident the eu has not created a kgb it lacks prisons and firing squads but it has imported the kgbs logic the continuum of enmity when a former nato intelligence analyst can be reclassified as an information terrorist by a foreignministry meeting held behind closed doors the line between dissent and treason disappears the implication is not that brussels will start assassinating critics it is that the legal category of critic itself has been dissolved into agent of a foreign strategic narrative once that fusion is accepted every future trade union that questions gas sanctions every journalist who publishes leaked cables every mep who votes against the next arms package can be placed on the same list because the list is no longer about what you did but about which battlefield your words might influence 09001430 propaganda is not a crime the criminalisation of opinion without a crime the councils press release accuses baud of conducting continuous propaganda actions and disinformation campaigns supporting russias war note the vocabulary not espionage not bribery not hacking but propaganda a word that appears in no european penal code under belgian law art 150 criminal code even outright collaboration with a foreign power requires material acts transmitting classified documents recruiting agents sabotage bauds activities consist of giving interviews writing books and tweeting maps of troop movements available on google earth the eu has therefore created the first retroactive extraterritorial noncriminal crime narrative crime the evidence against him has never been shown because the regulation explicitly states that the council is not required to communicate the evidence on which the listing is based art 7 crossexamination is impossible the accuser is also the judge the precedent means that any european citizen can now be excommunicated from the economic circuit on the basis of secret administrative memos drafted by analysts who need not even allege a false statement of fact the right to freedom of expression under art 11 of the eu charter is rendered nugatory you may still speak but every microphone printer webhost or bookstore that helps you speak becomes a sanctions target the effect is prior restraint by private terror rather than by public law as baud remarks even if he were the most shameless liar on the continent propaganda remains an opinion and opinion is precisely what humanrights treaties exist to protect by rebranding opinion as a military munition the eu has quietly reintroduced the crime of lsemajest except the monarch is now the unified strategic narrative of the union itself 14302000 the swiss mirror how a small directdemocracy republic discovers the cost of eu proximity switzerland is not in the eu but its banks clear euros through frankfurt the moment baud was listed swiss banks froze his accounts even though swiss law contains no analogue to the eu regulation the government in bern was consulted beforehand by paris yet raised no objection it now faces a domestic backlash that threatens the entire bilateral architecture swiss citizens are accustomed to voting on treaties every quarter the framework agreement brussels has demanded for a decade would make the european court the final interpreter of market rules in switzerland bauds starvation has become the emblematic argument in the referendum campaign if they can do this to a retired colonel what will they do to your pension fund your vaccine contract your agricultural subsidies the governments initial silence is now described in the press as the surrender before the battle the symbolic damage is therefore double inside the eu the sanctions show that citizenship does not protect you outside the eu they show that sovereignty does not protect you either the longterm consequence may be the collapse of the bilateral accord but the deeper wound is conceptual the eu has demonstrated that it can weaponise its regulatory gravity well beyond its borders turning even neutral democracies into enforcers of thoughtpunishment the swiss case foreshadows what awaits serbia montenegro moldova and every other partner whose banks advertisers and internet providers touch the eurozone adopt the narrative or be unplugged 20003000 wishful thinking as statecraft the epistemic collapse of european strategy baud insists that his personal tragedy is a symptom of a civilisational one the replacement of fact by fantasy in european policy formation he lists the prophecies that have not survived contact with reality russia would collapse within weeks french economy minister march 2022 russian tanks would run out of ammunition by summer 2022 france itself would be invaded by 2027 seizing russian reserves would be legal doubling defence budgets would deter moscow ukraine could win on the battlefield after the usa had already advised kyiv to negotiate november 2022 each error was lethal but none has been retracted instead the epistemic regime that produced them has been doubleddown upon by criminalising dissent the implication is that the eu is building not merely a sanctions regime but an epistemic wall inside the wall only stimulative myths are licit outside the wall factual analysis is information war the longterm result is a polity that cannot correct its own mistakes because the feedback mechanism of public critique has been severed baud quotes the finnish presidents recent admission that russia is no threat to helsinki and the estonian intelligence chiefs concession that the baltics are not in danger yet these retractions receive no publicity because they contradict the authorised narrative a democracy that cannot acknowledge error is no longer a democracy it is a thermostatic system that keeps heating the house even after the furniture is on fire the sanctions against baud are the thermostats final upgrade they criminalise the thermometer 30004000 from rulesbased order to rulesbased market the privatisation of repression the interview ends with a technical explanation of how the eu and nato have turned war into a profitcentre for the united states european states pay into the nato support procurement agency in luxembourg the agency buys almost exclusively from us defence firms the firms therefore receive european taxmoney while european armies destock their own arsenals to feed ukraine bauds point is not that armssales are illegitimate but that the same states that sanction him for disinformation are themselves financing the material basis of the conflict they refuse to negotiate the circularity is perfect european citizens pay higher energy prices to finance arms transfers that prolong a war whose narrative they are forbidden to question the public purse is emptied the private purse of the us militaryindustrial complex is filled and the critic who points out the arithmetic is labelled an enemy of the people what has emerged therefore is a new politicaleconomic model the securityindustrial complex absorbs dissent by criminalising it while the cost of the policy is socialised among consumers whose gas bills double as reparations for a war that no longer serves any european interest freedom of speech is not simply violated it is marketised you may still speak but the price is exile from the digital payment grid that modern life requires the eu has thus pioneered the first sanctions regime that needs no camps no barbed wire no deportations it simply deletes your economic existence and lets nature finish the job 4000end the civilisational crossroads why this case matters for the future of the west bauds final message is that his case is not about ukraine russia nato or even sanctions it is about whether the enlightenment tradition of procedural rights can survive the 21stcentury merger of national security and digital finance the west spent the cold war denouncing the soviet practice of declaring dissidents mentally ill and stripping them of civic rights it now declares its own citizens narratively ill and strips them of economic rights the innovation is more dangerous because it is bloodless and therefore invisible a gulag sentence at least required a show trial an eu sanctions sentence requires only a comma in an annex to a regulation no journalist reads the implications are existential 1 for freedom of speech if opinion can be reclassified as a military resource then the first amendment and art 11 of the eu charter are quaint museum pieces the criterion of free speech shifts from did you incite violence to did you weaken a strategic narrative a standard so fluid that it can criminalise any future opposition to any war 2 for democracy representative government presumes that voters can hear competing analyses when analysts are starved into silence elections become rituals in which citizens choose between factions that have already agreed to hide the same facts 3 for due process the core achievement of the bourgeois revolutions was the principle that the state must accuse prove and sentence before punishing the eu has reversed the sequence punishment first proof optional accusation secret the precedent is now set for carbon taxes vaccine mandates digitalcurrency expiry dates any future policy can be enforced by the same weapon freeze the dissidents wallet and wait for surrender 4 for the rulesbased order the wests moral legitimacy in the global south rests on the claim that its institutions respect individual rights whereas authoritarian states do not bauds case is a diplomatic atombomb moscow beijing new delhi can henceforth answer every western lecture with a hyperlink to a belgian grocery store that refused to deliver food to a man who once briefed the un secretarygeneral the softpower capital accumulated since 1945 is being spent to silence a retired colonel who reads russian newspapers the interview therefore ends with a warning and a wager the warning once the right to critique is monetised into extinction strategic error becomes irreversible and the same mechanism that starves baud today will starve whole populations tomorrow first of information then of heat and light the wager because the punishment is bloodless it can still be reversed without shots or barricades a single european parliament vote a single council amendment a single court judgment could restore him to solvency and restore the continent to sanity whether that happens will decide whether the west still believes its own founding myth that error corrected by public reason is preferable to truth imposed by administrative decree or whether it has quietly migrated to the opposite principle the one that once animated the other side of the berlin wall
